name: invalid-signature-count-over-the-ceiling
description: B18, the per-block signature ceiling MaxSigsPerBlock(T). T is seeded to 25000, one sixty-fourth of T0, so the ceiling is 93 and this block's 6 certificates declare 96 signatures between them. THE RULE IS CHECKED BEFORE ANY SIGNATURE IS VERIFIED, which is the whole of it: an implementation that counts after verifying has bounded nothing, and this block is the input that says so -- it costs a conforming node one linear pass over certificate headers and a non-conforming one 96 strict Ed25519 verifications. Every other ceiling that scales with T is clear: 67800 sequential gas against a 4T bound of 100000, above the 2T soft threshold of 50000, which is a forfeiture and not a rejection; 23698 bytes against 39062; 6 certificates against 62; and 70512 parallel gas against 150000 -- so B18 is the rule that rejects, not B5, B12 or B13. Every certificate is a RETIRE of fifteen one-shot addresses paying its deposit from a sixteenth, the gas-densest family the Era-0 program set admits; none is hand-rolled. THIS BLOCK USED TO BE THE CORPUS'S B5 VECTOR: the same family reaches 4T only by declaring far more signatures than this ceiling admits, so B18 answers first and B5 is no longer reachable on it. B5 remains a rule an implementation must enforce with no vector to catch it, like B11 and B16.

expect.reason: fold: invalid block: B18: 96 signatures exceeds the ceiling of 93
